l1: What is the exact issue being experienced by users?
Are there any error messages displayed to the user?
When did the issue first start occurring?
Have there been any recent changes in the environment like updates or hardware changes?
Is the issue constant or sporadic and intermittent?
Has any preliminary troubleshooting been done on the customer side?
Are there any known temporary workarounds being used?
Do workarounds include rebooting servers or disconnecting and reconnecting sessions?
l2: Is there a single Connection Broker or multiple brokers configured in High Availability?
When using multiple Connection Brokers in HA, how many brokers are configured?
Can you load the RDMS UI content on each Connection Broker successfully?
Has the SQL connection string been altered or has the SQL server been renamed?
Do you get error messages when loading the RDMS UI in Server Manager?
Are all RDS deployment servers added to the server pool in Server Manager?
Have all certificates been properly configured and trusted in the RDS deployment?
Can the same actions be performed using equivalent PowerShell cmdlets if RDMS UI fails?

l1: Is this an RDS environment or direct RDP connection scenario?
Where are the client and server machines hosted (on-premises or cloud)?
What roles and features are installed on the RDS server?
Since when have users been reporting this issue?
l2: What is the connection flow architecture? Is load balancing, MFA, or proxy involved?
Is the issue happening for internal users, external users, or both?
What is the behavior after disabling UDP transport for RDP?
What happens with other users on the same session host when one disconnects?

l1: Check basic network connectivity by pinging the server and testing port 3389
Check if you can sign in locally on the server to perform tests
Verify Remote Desktop Services service is in running state on the server
Check if Remote Desktop is enabled in the system properties
From the server console, try connecting to localhost via RDP
l2: Recreate the RDP listener if it is corrupted or misconfigured
Recreate the RDP listener certificate if authentication issues occur
Change the RDP port temporarily to test if port conflicts exist
Check if RD Gateway is configured and test behavior by bypassing the Gateway
Identify at which level the error occurs to determine the starting point for troubleshooting

l1: Check event logs while replicating the issue (System, Application)
Collect gpresult output to review Group Policy settings
Collect system information using the systeminfo command
l2: Collect RDS traces for detailed session and connection information
Capture a network trace during RDP connection attempts

rds_connection_failure.title: RDS connection fails or disconnects frequently

steps.action: Check Remote Desktop Services service status
Test network connectivity and port 3389 availability
steps.expect: Port blocked or network issues identified

steps.action: Restart RDS service and recreate RDP listener
Test RDP connection and monitor Event Viewer
steps.expect: Connection stable with no new errors
